story-summary.user-story: As a system, I want to send proactive messages to users via Telegram, so that trigger messages reach users through their preferred channel.
story-summary.description: This story implements the delivery mechanism for sending proactive AI-generated messages to users via Telegram. It provides a clean interface for the wake-up agent to deliver messages, handles rate limits gracefully, and manages errors without crashing the background worker.

criterion.title: Delivery Function
criterion.then: - Looks up user's Telegram chat_id from Redis/profile - Sends message via Telegram Bot API - Returns message_id for tracking

criterion.title: Rate Limit Handling
criterion.then: - Respects 429 responses - Implements exponential backoff - Retries up to 3 times

criterion.title: Error Handling
criterion.then: - Returns None for message_id - Logs error with context - Does not crash worker

architecture.overview: Annie's Telegram bot already has full infrastructure for receiving and sending messages. This story adds a delivery module that allows the proactive worker to send messages to users by reusing the existing Telegram bot infrastructure.

telegram-bot-structure.description: The Telegram bot service runs as a separate Docker container (telegram-bot) with long polling. It uses the python-telegram-bot library and communicates with the backend via HTTP.

key-files.file: Main bot initialization and polling setup
Message handlers with rate limit handling

option.name: Direct Bot API
option.description: Create delivery module in backend that directly calls Telegram Bot API using bot token. This is the recommended approach for proactive messaging.
option.pros: - Independent of bot polling process - Can send messages from background worker - Full control over rate limiting and retries - No need to route through telegram-bot service
option.implementation: Create backend/api/proactive/delivery.py that uses python-telegram-bot's Bot class directly to send messages. The Bot class handles HTTP API calls to Telegram servers.

option.name: Via Telegram Bot Service
option.description: Add HTTP endpoint to telegram-bot service for sending messages
option.cons: - Requires adding HTTP server to telegram-bot service (currently only has polling) - Adds architectural complexity - Not recommended for background worker pattern

chat-id-lookup.description: Telegram requires a chat_id to send messages to users. The chat_id is the Telegram user ID, which is captured when users first interact with the bot.

current-storage.note: The user_id in our system IS the Telegram chat_id (see message handler). When users send messages, update.message.from_user.id becomes the user_id. This is passed to backend in ChatRequest as user_id (string format).
current-storage.evidence: user_id = message.from_user.id # This is the Telegram user ID chat_id = message.chat_id # For 1-on-1 chats, same as user_id

chat-id-lookup.implementation-approach:
Since user_id in our system is already the Telegram chat_id (as string), we can use it directly for message delivery. No additional lookup needed.
For safety, we should: 1. Store platform="telegram" in session (already done in state.py) 2. Use user_id directly as chat_id (convert to int) 3. Handle case where user_id might be from different platform (future-proofing)

retry-logic.backoff-strategy: - On RetryAfter exception, wait retry_error.retry_after seconds - If no retry_after, use exponential: 2 ** (attempt - 1) - Log each retry attempt with context

task.title: Add error handling
task.description: Wrap in try/except and log errors gracefully

error-types.error: Rate limit - handled by retry logic
Invalid parameters - log and return failure
General API error - log and return failure
Unexpected error - log with exc_info and return failure

task.logging-pattern: logger.error( "Failed to deliver message to Telegram", extra={ "user_id": user_id, "message_preview": message[:50], # First 50 chars "error": str(e), "error_type": type(e).__name__, "event": "telegram_delivery_failed" }, exc_info=True )
task.graceful-degradation: All errors should return DeliveryResult(success=False, message_id=None, error=str(e)) Never raise exceptions - the worker must continue running

dev-notes.note: User_id in our system IS the Telegram chat_id. This is because when users send messages to the bot, the Telegram user ID (from_user.id) becomes our user_id. So no separate lookup is needed - just convert string to int.

The Bot class from python-telegram-bot can be used independently of the Application (polling) setup. This allows the backend to send messages without interfering with the telegram-bot service's polling loop.
Consider adding a message queue for retries if delivery fails. This could be implemented in a future story (similar to memory_queue pattern in memory.py).
For multi-platform support in the future, add platform validation and routing logic. Could store platform-specific chat identifiers in user profile or session.
